entries.title: All Things Policy | How Is The Iran War Impacting US Midterms?
entries.description: In this episode of All Things Policy, Vanshika Saraf and Abhishek Kadiyala examine what the war on Iran means for the November 2026 midterm elections in the U.S. The joint U.S. and Israeli strikes that began on 28 February 2026 have not become a campaign issue in their own right, with only 4 per cent of Americans naming foreign policy as their top concern by July. The conversation applies a test drawn from Iraq in 2002 and Afghanistan in 2010, which is that American wars seldom rank as voter priorities yet often worsen the issues that do. The episode works through the evidence, including inflation at 4.2 per cent, petrol at USD 4.65 a gallon, record-low congressional approval of 10 per cent, and the repeated collapse of War Powers Resolution votes. entries.title: #26 Institutional Mistrust: The Second 'i'
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: The second of the four 'i'ssues that could determine the fate of 2026 US mid-terms.

entries.title: #25 Inflation: The First 'i'
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: The first of the four 'i'ssues that could influence the US mid-terms.

entries.title: #23 Gerrymandering and the New Rules of US Politics
entries.author: Brigadier Anil Raman
entries.description: The Supreme Court’s Louisiana v. Callais decision weakens protections against electoral maps that dilute minority voting power, making it harder to challenge districts through intent-based rather than outcome-based standards. The piece analyses how both parties increasingly treat redistricting as a partisan tool, drawing comparisons to India’s independent delimitation system.

entries.title: Why The Blockade Is Trump's Best Card
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Abhishek Kadiyala argues that a naval blockade of Iran is the Trump administration's strategically optimal move — it avoids triggering the 60-day War Powers Resolution clock while maintaining pressure, keeping congressional hawks satisfied and doves outmanoeuvred.

entries.title: Analysing US Congressional Oversight on the Iran War
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: This policy brief examines congressional responses to President Trump's military action against Iran, which began February 28, 2026. The analysis explores two institutional mechanisms through which Congress can exercise oversight: the War Powers Resolution (WPR) and budgetary appropriations authority. The brief identifies deep partisan and intra-party divisions, tracks multiple failed legislative attempts, and concludes that budgetary restraint represents Congress's most viable constraint mechanism.

entries.title: #21 — A Generational Mid-term?
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: At least one in eight members of Congress is departing ahead of the 2026 midterms — the highest retirement rate since 1992. The piece examines the three forces driving the exodus: institutional frustration with a gridlocked Congress, deepening partisan polarisation that makes legislating increasingly thankless, and a declining appeal of federal service relative to state-level or private-sector alternatives.

entries.title: 35 US Lawmakers Just Moved A Bill That Could Upend Indian Techies' Careers
entries.author: Brigadier Anil Raman
entries.description: Brigadier Anil Raman examines a bipartisan congressional bill, co-sponsored by 35 House members, that would tighten H-1B visa rules and add domestic hiring requirements — legislation that directly affects Indian technology professionals and reflects the populist electoral pressures shaping Congress ahead of the 2026 midterms.

entries.title: The Iran Brief: US Congress and Trump
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala, Brigadier Anil Raman & Soren Dayton
entries.description: With the 60-day War Powers Resolution clock ticking, this episode examines why Congress has again failed to constrain Trump's military operations against Iran. The panel unpacks the structural weaknesses of the War Powers Resolution — including the Trump administration filing only classified reports. The core argument: the real obstacle is political will, not legal ambiguity.

entries.title: Three Things May Happen At The End Of The 14-Day Ceasefire (Or Earlier)
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Kadiyala maps three possible trajectories as the US-brokered Iran ceasefire nears its deadline: a negotiated settlement, a return to hostilities requiring fresh congressional authorisation, or an ambiguous freeze that leaves war powers questions unresolved.

entries.title: The Iran Brief: Why Is US Congress Failing To Stop Trump On Iran?
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala & Bhumika Sevkani
entries.description: Congress has repeatedly failed to constrain President Trump's military actions against Iran despite multiple legislative attempts. The episode traces failed resolutions invoking the War Powers Resolution of 1973 — sponsored by Tim Kaine, Thomas Massie, Ro Khanna, and Chris Murphy — and examines how partisanship, electoral incentives, and ideological splits (cutting across party lines) have shaped outcomes.

entries.title: #19 The “March-uary” of Iran War Bills
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: How and why has the Congress failed to stop Trump’s war in Iran

entries.title: All Things Policy | The Iran Brief: War and MAGA Fissures
entries.author: Lokendra Sharma & Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Takshashila Institution's All Things Policy examines the fissures within the MAGA coalition in Congress over the Iran strikes, and what the split reveals about Congress’s capacity — and willingness — to constrain the executive on war powers.

entries.title: If Trump Puts Troops In Iran
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Kadiyala examines the constitutional and political consequences of deploying US ground forces to Iran, including how the War Powers Resolution would be triggered, what bipartisan opposition in Congress looks like, and why the 60-day clock becomes Trump's most immediate legislative constraint.

entries.title: All Things Policy — US Congress, War Powers & Iran
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala & Brigadier Anil Raman
entries.description: An episode of All Things Policy examining the US Congress's role and response in the context of military action, war powers, and the legislative dynamics of the current Congress.

entries.title: The system bends, it rarely breaks, says U.S. Congressional expert Matthew Glassman
entries.author: Brigadier Anil Raman
entries.description: Brigadier Anil Raman interviews Matthew Glassman, a leading expert on US Congressional procedure, who argues that despite Trump-era stress tests, American democratic institutions — particularly Congressional checks on executive power — are resilient by design, though not invulnerable.

entries.title: #18 Why and How Has Congress Responded Differently to Venezuela, Greenland, and Iran?
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Dossier in Brief: comparing the legislative responses to three distinct foreign policy crises and what the divergence reveals about congressional incentives.

entries.title: There Are Two Big Problems Trump May Run Into If He Actually Attacks Iran
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Kadiyala identifies two structural obstacles to Trump striking Iran: the War Powers Resolution's 60-day constraint and the fractured Republican coalition in Congress, where fiscal hawks and libertarian-leaning members resist open-ended military commitments without explicit authorisation.

entries.title: How Congress, Pentagon contain POTUS overreach and how India should leverage it
entries.author: Brigadier Anil Raman
entries.description: Brigadier Anil Raman analyses the constitutional and institutional mechanisms — Congressional appropriations authority, the War Powers Resolution, and senior military leadership — that constrain presidential overreach, and argues India should deepen ties with both Congress and the Pentagon rather than treat the White House as the sole interlocutor.

entries.title: #13 DC Dossier 2025 Recap
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: A year-end review of how the 119th Congress engaged with India-related legislation, hearings, and bilateral policy debates across 2025.

entries.title: #11 Partisan Divides and Strategic Expectations
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Key takeaways from the House hearing on the US–India strategic partnership, analysing how partisan lines shaped members’ priorities and the divergence between Democratic and Republican expectations of the relationship.

entries.title: #10 End of the Shutdown. Who Won and Lost
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Analysing the end of the longest government shutdown in United States history — which members and factions gained leverage, which lost it, and what the resolution signals for the 119th Congress’s governing capacity.

entries.title: #9 Trump’s Economic Policies Devastate His Base, Fuel Democratic Rout, and Imperil Midterms
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: How the Trump administration’s economic policies — tariffs, spending cuts, and fiscal pressure — have translated into a Democratic sweep in off-cycle elections and what the trend implies for the 2026 midterms.

entries.title: #5 Understanding US Government Shutdown
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: DCD Brief: the causes, key legislative flashpoints, and likely duration of the 2025 US government shutdown — and what it reveals about dysfunction in the 119th Congress.

entries.title: House lessons for Trump
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Kadiyala draws on the institutional history of the House of Representatives to argue that Trump's legislative strategy underestimates the chamber's capacity for obstruction — and that the thin Republican majority and fractious Freedom Caucus will prove a recurring constraint on the administration's domestic agenda heading into 2026.

entries.title: #4 Democracy First: The House’s Consensus on Pakistan Policy
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: How does the 119th US House of Representatives view Pakistan? An analysis of bipartisan consensus — and its limits — on democracy conditionality, military aid, and human rights benchmarks in House engagement with Islamabad.

entries.author: Brigadier Anil Raman
entries.description: US foreign policy: Trump's Iran agreement signals a shift in Republican foreign policy shaped by domestic politics and the America First movement overturning traditional alliance hierarchies and prioritising electoral calculations in West Asia policy.

entries.title: Trump’s Cuba Gamble Could Spiral Beyond US Control
entries.author: Brigadier Anil Raman
entries.description: Trump’s Cuba blockade strategy risks military escalation, refugee crises, and global backlash as Russia and China back Havana. Read the full analysis.

entries.author: Brigadier Anil Raman

entries.author: Brigadier Anil Raman
entries.description: Trump’s Dallas convention highlights rising US protectionism amid H-1B visa changes and BRICS summit. India must diversify alliances as American domestic politics grows unpredictable and mercantile, say experts.

entries.title: Loony Left, Radical Right & India-US
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Throughout the tumultuous second Trump presidency, the 119th session of United States Congress has proven to be a relatively consistent element in India-US ties. In this session, Congress has introduced pro-India legislation, pigeonholed critical bills, prioritised India as an irreplaceable partner against China, and funded several US-India partnership initiatives, including programmes under Quad.
